comparator.name: Public Governance (English variant)
comparator.sourceNotes: Registry row 240 identifies the English-language Public Governance variant, distinct from the Dutch Bestuurskunde target CP220. The current programme admissions page identifies Dutch delivery, and adopted 2026–2027 programme-specific Appendix 1a Article 4 confirms Dutch with individual English-language units permitted. Historical 2022–2023 regulations record closure of the English Public Governance track to new entrants from 2020–2021. The department overview still mentions the English BSc, but current admissions and adopted regulations control entrant availability. No Dutch curriculum is relabelled as a current English pathway.

programmes.label: Public Governance (English variant) at Tilburg University

exception.reason: The normalized target is the English-language Public Governance bachelor variant. Current admissions and adopted regulations establish the Dutch-taught Bestuurskunde bachelor instead; the former English track closed to new entrants from 2020–2021. The prior comparison assigned the Dutch programme curriculum to this English variant. This is a target-identity conflict, not an academic no-match with UCR.
exception.curriculumContext: No current English-entry 180-EC pathway is certified for this target. The current Dutch programme is separately reviewed as CP220. Historical English-track courses and the current Dutch curriculum are not combined or presented as a new English cohort.

audience.programmeDescription: Public Governance was an English-language track of Tilburg University’s public-administration bachelor. The current Bestuurskunde bachelor is taught in Dutch, with some courses offered in English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A current English-language pathway is not available for this registry variant: Tilburg closed the English track to new entrants from 2020–2021. No UCR comparison is shown for this entry. The separately listed Dutch Public Administration programme has its own comparison.

curriculum.limitation: The former English track must not be confused with the current Dutch-taught programme.
